{"id":"vouch-xlha.20","title":"check: replaying an old tier record undoes a demotion","description":"Restoring an earlier signed tier record undoes a demotion with no warning.

Where (HEAD 4237c43): git-vouch:1787-1860 judge_tier, and History.added at 1161-1177. Authority is judged at the commit that (re)added the bytes; nothing compares the record with the one it replaces.

Reproduced with real git and ssh-keygen (scratchpad a1/replay.sh):
1. linus (anchor) approves alice as maintainer (T1), commit.
2. linus approves alice as contributor (T2), commit. check: "alice contributor".
3. Anyone copies T1's tiers/alice.json and .sig back and commits. check: "alice maintainer", exit 0, no warning or void. `export --min-tier maintainer` lists alice with no valid-before.

Why it matters: DESIGN.md "Merging needs one person" says tier records are signed so a merger cannot forge one, and lists only three review-gated risks (anchors.json, unsigned person changes, tier deletions). A replay has the same effect as a forged grant: the demoted person (or a merger) restores a tier the approver withdrew, and check gives the merger no signal. The replayed record's `date` is older than the record it replaces, and nothing looks at that.

Fix: when a tier record replaces a verified earlier one (any version standing at a parent of the adding commit), require its `date` to be strictly later than that record's `date`. Otherwise report a problem, or a void plus a WARNING naming the replay. That rejects byte-identical replays and also backdated replacements (see the peer-demotion bead). A content check (bytes seen in an ancestor version) also catches exact replays, but misses an old record re-signed by a key whose holder is no longer trusted. Either way, add the case to the list of review-gated risks in DESIGN.md if it stays a warning.
